items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: French people, Edith Piaf and all of them, they like to sing low.

ctx.x: You've got to watch your audience and see what they want. And you'll catch them at a different time, and you might they come in there and want, "Toot, Toot, Tootsie, Goodbye". You've got an audience like that, you want to give them how they feel. And I've found that that can be used today. A lot of times, a lot of people use the wrong things on the wrong people at the time.

Like, I heard Barbra Streisand sing "Mon Homme". But, where it was, it was the wrong place for it, you know what I mean? And then, she was singing a song that wasn't very good for her, anyhow. For this reason. French people, Edith Piaf and all of them, they like to sing low. And [Streisand] she was too high. Like in, "Mon Homme", she has a nice beautiful voice, but that was a question of the wrong song, what I'm trying to bring out.
